state.goal: Choose coherent v1 boundaries for an AI-written, token-efficient CRUD business SaaS DSL. Adoption is primary. No compiler/runtime exists yet. Prefer one canonical primitive, no per-app infrastructure boilerplate. Runtime is workerd; Cloudflare services, PatternFly HTML/CSS and MCP are first class. # above any declaration is its canonical description; ## is a code comment.
evidence: 35 drafts include CRM, invoices, stock, reservations, approvals and team tasks. Some earlier observability drafts are explicitly outside supported scope. A language specification must not silently implement free-form English effects.

Each package owns one Given/When/Then. Small apps use implicit main; multiple packages can share a file or be separate. One app deployment and MCP endpoint. Root app context declares runtime/auth/teams/bindings once.

Existing policy write rules duplicate CRUD by predicates and conflict with legitimate scenario-controlled fields. Read policies may differ by role or record and field. Custom scenarios must not inherit arbitrary generic CRUD writable fields.
Some aggregate/read results intentionally expose a statistic without exposing raw rows. Others must respect viewer row and field permissions. Ambiguous implicit privilege is unacceptable.

PatternFly HTML/CSS is available, but React charts and complete drag/drop calendars are not automatically HTML/CSS components. Language targets ordinary business apps; arbitrary HTML, CSS and JS are not required.

D1 is default. An optional Durable Object should own a related model group, including canonical CRUD, guards, receipts and jobs. Cross-owner atomic commits cannot be promised. A DO mirror is not authoritative.
Canonical low-level create/set effects are necessary for business workflows. Implicit snapshot/freeze/history/immutable variants currently overlap. Generated audit history already exists.

MCP operations share authorization with UI. Team context must always be validated; models and schemas cannot guess team or identity from tool inputs. Browser users may switch teams through the generated shell. OAuth consent can select a team.

permissions.instructions: Choose the simplest permission decomposition that supports realistic approval workflows without duplicate authorization declarations.

criteria.read_plus_operations: Model policy defines readable rows/fields; CRUD by plus field lists and scenario by define allowed writes. All writes still check tenant scope, typed relations and invariants. Returned data always requires read permission.
criteria.read_write_plus_operations: Model policy defines read and write ceilings; each CRUD/scenario also defines by. Scenarios changing otherwise protected fields need an explicit additional privileged-write rule.

authority.instructions: Choose canonical source ownership for optional Durable Object-backed data.

criteria.model: A model declares at=Authority, descendants inherit; all operations infer the owner. Mixing owner instances in one mutation fails. No per-operation atomic block.
criteria.operation: Every operation selects atomic at=Authority and compiler checks model consistency; CRUD must repeat that selection.

presentation.instructions: Choose a bounded v1 presentation catalog suitable for ordinary target business apps.

criteria.composed: Lists/tables/forms/cards plus enum-grouped card boards, date-grouped agenda calendars, metrics/history. No drag/drop, rich text, arbitrary HTML/CSS/JS or React chart dependencies. Fixed theme/layout options.
criteria.base_only: Only lists/tables/forms/cards in v1; defer boards, calendars and metrics even as simple compositions.
criteria.full_freedom: Include arbitrary HTML/CSS/JS as an escape hatch for missing UI behavior.

mcp_team.instructions: Choose MCP team context for scoped business operations.

criteria.connection: OAuth connection selects and binds one team. All tool calls revalidate membership. A different team requires a separate/re-authorized connection. Tool schemas omit repeated team arguments.
criteria.argument: Every business tool accepts a team identifier, revalidated each call. One connection may operate across teams.

freeze_snapshot.instructions: Choose a canonical way to preserve submitted values and prevent subsequent changes without overlapping primitives.

criteria.explicit_copy_lock: Use create/set with typed structural values for snapshots; one declarative lock Model fields=... when=predicate evaluated on pre-state blocks later edits. Automatic audit history, no separate snapshot/freeze/immutable verbs.
criteria.runtime_verbs: Provide separate snapshot and freeze effects plus immutable declarations, precisely define their overlaps and retained-field behavior.

query_privilege.instructions: Choose an explicit rule for private state needed by business guards and authorized aggregate reports.

criteria.split_context: Pure read scenarios run as viewer by default; explicit scope=authority allows intentionally declassified typed results. Mutation guards/effects can inspect authority state but returned records still project permissions; arbitrary private scalar returns require an explicit declared report/output grant.
criteria.viewer_everywhere: All queries use caller read policies, including guards and invariants; runtime must separately recover full authority state for specific built-in invariants.
criteria.authority_everywhere: Every scenario can query full tenant data and return arbitrary scalar results; scenario by alone grants all resulting information.

draft_migration.instructions: Choose the honest deliverable for finalizing language design when 35 legacy drafts contain unresolved application-specific pseudo-operations and no compiler exists.

criteria.spec_examples: Finish a normative v1 language/runtime contract and a few concrete reference examples; explicitly mark legacy drafts as needing migration. Do not claim they compile or fulfill app requirements.
criteria.rewrite_all: Translate all 35 drafts now before freezing design, accepting substantial additional business-logic work and no executable validation.
criteria.keep_ambiguous: Preserve existing draft syntax as valid even where semantics are undefined, for source compatibility.
